extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD managers, analysts, cost accountants, and researchers performing OMB Circular A-76 cost comparisons and evaluating in-house vs contract MIS (HRMIN) operations
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 cost comparison for HRMIN
extracted.subtask_description: Conducting a cost-comparison study, per OMB Circular No. A-76, to determine whether the Navy's HRMIN in-house operations or contracting-out (timesharing/service bureau) is the most cost‑effective alternative. The work lays out scope, cost element accumulation, contract cost development, benchmarking, life‑cycle considerations, and NPV analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OMB Circular No. A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an in-house development/service is in accordance with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) policy on acquiring commercial or industrial products and services (OMB Circular No. A-76, 5 April 1979). The policy requires review of each commercial or industrial activity costing more than $100,000 to decide if existing in-house or contract performance continues to comply with the policy and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost comparison and conclusions must be based on application of the requirements of OMB Circular No. A-76; the methodology of the study should be 'laid out as specified in OMB Circular No. A-76.' Use the Circular's procedures and thresholds (e.g., $100,000 review threshold) when framing scope and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope definition (including benchmarking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the scope of the review: identify the activity to be reviewed (HRMIN at NPRDC), the boundaries of the analysis, and any benchmarking to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis includes a 'SCOPE' section and explicitly references 'Benchmarking' as part of scope determination. Scope must show why HRMIN meets A-76 guidelines for review and identify what installations, functions, and costs are included or excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use benchmarking to compare current in-house performance against alternative locations or service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarking is used as an explicit part of the scope (see Table of Contents: 'Benchmarking'). Use comparable operations/locations or commercial service rates as benchmarks to validate cost and performance assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative assessment: in-house versus contract-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly evaluate alternative performance arrangements — e.g., Alternative One: HRMIN at NPRDC (in-house) versus Alternative Two: computer service bureaus (contract-out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out each alternative's characteristics, costs, benefits, and disadvantages. The study organizes the comparison into named alternatives (Part D and E) and evaluates typical charges, benefits, and disadvantages of service bureaus vs in-house operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost element identification and accumulation (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and accumulate all relevant cost elements for in-house performance before comparing to contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed cost-element approach as in Part F: list and quantify direct and indirect costs, overhead, G&A, capital, inflation, one-time costs, etc., to produce a comprehensive in-house cost accumulation (see 'Summary of Part F').

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for direct labor costs associated with in-house operation (salaries/wages for personnel performing HRMIN tasks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Labor is identified as a primary cost element (see '1. Direct Labor' under Part F). Use actual FY data where possible (e.g., 'HRMIN (FY 1982) Direct Labor Costs').

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits on Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Include fringe benefit costs on labor (e.g., employer-paid benefits) as part of annual labor costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fringe benefits are treated as a separate cost element (see '2. Fringe Benefits on Labor (FY 82) Annual Labor Costs'). Accurately estimate fringe percentages and apply consistently to direct labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations Overhead Expenses (with components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accumulate operations overhead expenses, including indirect labor; indirect materials and supplies; depreciation; rent; maintenance and repair; support costs; utilities; insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F lists multiple subcomponents under 'Operations Overhead Expenses' (a–h). Each subcomponent must be identified, quantified, and justified (e.g., depreciation schedules, rent equivalents, utility allocations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and include other direct costs (non-labor direct expenditures) tied to in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as '4. Other Direct Costs' in Part F; include items like consumables, travel, special software, contractor support that are directly attributable to HRMIN operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General and Administrative Expenses (G&A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an allocation of general and administrative expenses associated with in-house operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G&A is a recognized cost element ('5. General and Administrative Expenses (G & A)'). Use appropriate allocation bases and document the rationale for G&A rates applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider inflation effects on recurring costs over the analysis period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inflation is explicitly listed ('6. Inflation'); when projecting multi-year costs (e.g., 5‑year life), adjust nominal costs appropriately and document inflation assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of Capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Include cost of capital components when they are material to comparing in-house and contract alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F lists '7. Cost of Capital'. For government analyses, cost of capital may be treated as an imputed opportunity cost; justify the rate and treatment used.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Time Costs and Other Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for one-time implementation or transition costs and any other non-recurring costs in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include set-up, conversion, training, and other one-time expenditures ('8. One-Time Costs and Other Costs'). Capitalize or expense per policy and ensure parity between alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting-out: contract cost development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the contract-out (service bureau/timesharing) cost estimate using typical charges and adjustments for the user profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G ('CONTRACTING-OUT, CONTRACT COST DEVELOPMENT') describes constructing contract costs by determining user profiles, applying typical charges, adjusting for benefits/disadvantages, and summarizing contract performance cost accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: User profile determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the user profile (usage pattern, resource needs) to compute contract-out costs accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Part G ('1. User Profile Determination' and 'a. Computations'), define user access patterns, CPU/time estimates, storage, and timesharing needs; document computational steps used to convert profile into charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical charges, benefits, and disadvantages of service bureaus/timesharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify typical service bureau/time-sharing charges and weigh typical benefits and disadvantages in the contract-out alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E includes '1. Typical Charges', '2. Typical Benefits', '3. Typical Disadvantages'. List unit charges, value propositions (lower telecom cost, scalability), and negative factors (loss of control, security, provider reliability). Adjust contract costs for these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Present Value / Present Value Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use present value (net present value) analysis to compare multi-year costs of alternatives on a common time-and-cost basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix F and the NPV discussion prescribe discounting future cash flows. Guidance includes: the government treats the discount rate as an opportunity cost (example: 10% discount rate); assume equal useful life for alternatives (e.g., five years); discount recurring tangible costs; note that government cannot 'bank' money so interpretation of return differs; include sensitivity to tax offsets (2%), contract management cost (4%), and comment on materiality of intangible costs (insurance, cost of capital). Document assumptions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions for NPV and analysis horizon
rubrics_metrics.description: Make and document assumptions about analysis horizon, asset lives, recurring costs stability, discount rate, and treatment of intangibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix F shows assumptions: equal five-year life for alternatives, recurring variable tangible costs assumed unchanged year-to-year, use of a 10% discount rate as imputed opportunity cost, income tax offset of 2% considered immaterial, and 4% contract management cost used to amplify results. State and justify these assumptions and test sensitivity where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life-Cycle Management of Automated Information Systems (AIS) — five phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider AIS life-cycle phases when evaluating systems: Mission Analysis/Project Initiation; Concept Development; Definition/Design; System Development; Deployment/Operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis references SECNAVINST 5231.1A and lists the five life-cycle phases; analysis should account for costs and responsibilities across the life cycle (see Appendix A). Ensure alternatives are compared on equivalent life-cycle stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of OMB Circular A-76 (procedural steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the procedural steps and implementation guidance for applying OMB Circular A-76 to a specific activity review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix D (Implementation of OMB Circular A-76) is referenced; apply the Circular's step-by-step procedural requirements (solicitation, bid analysis, cost comparison methodology, policy compliance) when executing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology assumptions and multidisciplinary techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: State methodological approach and acknowledge multidisciplinary techniques (managerial/cost accounting, economics, behavioral sciences, computer science, MIS) and any required prior knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology is 'straightforward' and 'laid out as specified in OMB Circular No. A-76.' The author notes that techniques/terms from multiple disciplines are used and some prior understanding is assumed. Explicitly state methodological limits, required competencies, and where specialist inputs are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of MIS benefits and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess qualitative benefits of the MIS (HRMIN) such as real-time management control, time savings, standardized report generation, electronic mail, database and research capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter III describes 'Why HRMIN' including 'MISs and Time', 'Real-Time Management Control', and 'Benefits of MISs.' When comparing costs, include qualitative benefits (management control, improved responsiveness, research tools like SPSS, standardized reporting) as part of the decision context and discuss how/if to quantify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative location assessment (location summary matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an assessment matrix to summarize and compare alternative locations or hosting options for the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 6 is 'Alternative Location Summary Assessment Matrix'; use structured matrices to compare factors (cost, capabilities, connectivity, geographic coverage) across alternatives and document weighting/scoring if applied.
